with the highest activity focused near Cape Fairweather.

exercise additional caution through this morning until this

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 27 at 9:39AM CDT until September 27 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
At 939 AM CDT /839 AM MDT/, a severe thunderstorm was located near
Bush's Landing, or 25 miles west of Onida, moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Golf ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Little Bend Rec Area around 940 AM CDT.
Bush's Landing around 950 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm is capable of producing
dangerous hail and damaging winds.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 27 at 10:11AM AST until September 27 at 4:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose

much of central and southern Utah between Monday morning and early
Tuesday morning.

creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and

Forsyth, and Silver King.

Pacific draws into portions of central and southern Utah on
Monday. Concurrently, an upper-level system traversing the Desert

widespread heavy rainfall across the area. Isolated heavier
storms will be capable of producing rainfall rates in excess of 1
inch per hour at times.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 27 at 9:17AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage and is
actively cresting due to an ongoing period of northerly winds and
tidal effects. River levels are forecast to gradually subside through
Minor Flood Stage this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Sunday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to crest around 2.7 feet today.
The river is then forecast to slowly subside through Minor Flood
Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 4:52AM PDT until September 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, minor tidal overflow
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late tonight.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Monday to 5 PM PDT
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and minor coastal erosion
expected during high tides. Additionally, elevated surf will
lead to strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-5 feet expected. Local
sets to 7 feet possible on south-facing beaches. Morning high
tides are expected to peak between 6.7 and 7.0 feet through
Wednesday, peaking Tuesday morning. The listed tide predictions
have been corrected to reflect current trends in actual tide
observations.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Chesapeake; Hampton/Poquoson; Suffolk; Norfolk; Portsmouth
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 6:51AM EDT until September 27 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Chesapeake and Suffolk, and Hampton/Poquoson, Norfolk
and Portsmouth Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon EDT today.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON EDT TODAY

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Currituck
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 27 at 6:51AM EDT until September 27 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, high rip current risk.

* WHERE...Eastern Currituck County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon EDT today.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Widespread flooding of vulnerable areas will result
in an elevated threat of property damage to homes and
businesses near the waterfront and shoreline. Water will be
around two feet above ground level in some areas resulting in
a sufficient depth to close numerous roads and threaten homes
and businesses. Flooding will extend inland from the
waterfront along tidal rivers and bays resulting in some road
closures and flooding of vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 27 at 6:46AM EDT until September 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of inundation
above ground level low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways with compromised dune structures. Elevated water
levels due to high astronomical tides and moderate west winds
may lead to localized minor flooding of low-lying areas prone to
soundside flooding. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents, large breaking waves, and hazardous debris
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks ocean-side locales that experienced
weakening of dune structures over the last few days. For soundside
localized flooding, low-lying areas prone to sound-side
flooding in and near Manteo.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until midnight EDT
tonight. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
with compromised dune structures resulting in a low threat of
property damage. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The next oceanside high tide times are
around 8:15 AM Sunday, and 8:30 PM Sunday. The soundside high
times are around 11:30 AM Sunday and midnight Sunday night. The
most likely time for strong rip currents to occur is a couple
hours either side of low tide, which will occur around 2:30 PM
Sunday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Watch out for debris that may be in the water.

properties.description:

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even

properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Southwest Suffolk; Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 27 at 6:02AM EDT until September 27 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 2 1/2 feet of
inundation above ground level in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront and shoreline. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the High
Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southwest Suffolk and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline. Flooding could again extend inland into coastal
areas that typically don't experience coastal flooding.
Coastal flooding will be exacerbated along north facing
shorelines from wave action, particularly for the barrier
island from Atlantic Beach, Long Beach to Jones Beach. This
will result in numerous road closures and cause widespread
flooding of low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the
waterfront. Vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded.

* SHOREFRONT AND BEACH IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet
along with elevated water levels will result in widespread
dune erosion and beach flooding. Localized overwashes are
possible where dune structures are compromised, resulting in
some flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind
protective dunes. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Life threatening rip currents are
likely for all people entering the surf zone.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through

properties.areaDesc: Atlantic Coastal Cape May; Coastal Atlantic
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 27 at 4:51AM EDT until September 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 1 to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the
High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Atlantic Coastal Cape May and Coastal Atlantic.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 PM EDT this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.
Breaching of sand dunes is possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.description:

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Aguila Valley, Apache Junction/Gold Canyon, Cave Creek/New
River, Deer Valley, Dripping Springs, Fountain Hills/East Mesa,
Globe/Miami, Mazatzal Mountains, New River Mesa, Northwest Valley,

Southeast Gila County, Superior and Tonto Basin.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

from the south and an approaching weather disturbance from the
west will result in showers and thunderstorms capable of
producing localized heavy rainfall. Moderate to heavy rainfall

will see training of storms leading to heavier rainfall
accumulations.

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

north winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt.

* WHEN...Small Craft Advisory, until 5 AM PDT early this
morning. Small Craft Advisory, from 2 PM this afternoon to 8
PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ebb current of 4.88 kt at 531 AM Sunday.
Seas 3 to 4 ft. Strong ebb current of 5.98 kt at 549 PM Sunday. Seas
5 to 6 ft. Ebb current of 4.64 kt at 606 AM Monday. Seas 6 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 1:39AM MDT until September 30 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Areas along and west of the central mountain chain
including the west slopes of the Sangre de Cristo's, the
Sandia/Manzano Mountains, and the south-central mountains, as well
as the Rio Grande Valley westward to the Arizona border. Some metro
areas and locales include, Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Espanola, Taos,
Socorro, Ruidoso, Los Alamos, Grants, Gallup, and Farmington.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A near-record to record surge of monsoonal moisture combined with
two merging storm systems will bring a prolonged multi- day
period of showers and thunderstorms producing moderate to heavy
rainfall. Combined with already rain soaked ground conditions,
there is a high risk of flash flooding.
- Low-lying, poorly drained areas, urban areas and arroyo systems
will be most susceptible. Near rivers and streams will see rises,
potentially reaching flood stage. Recent burn scars including the
Ruidoso area burn scars, Frijoles, Sacaton, Hummingbird, and
Whiskey burn scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 27 at 3:19AM EDT until September 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to one foot of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways (3.9 to 12.6 feet Mean Lower
Low Water). For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves
of 6 to 15 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Suffolk MA, Eastern Norfolk MA,
Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes MA and Nantucket MA
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong northeast winds with large waves will result
in minor coastal flooding with pockets of moderate coastal
flooding over multiple high tide cycles from late today
through the weekend. The water also may struggle to vacate the
area after the high tides given persistent strong northeast
winds. The greatest risk for coastal flooding appears to be
setting up south of Boston and onto the Cape and Islands. In
addition...the long duration of northeast winds coupled with
large waves over multiple high tide cycles will result in
areas of severe beach erosion for a prolonged period.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 27 at 2:25AM EDT until September 28 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf with breaking waves
of 3 to 6 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 26 at 7:27PM PDT until September 29 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf
Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Focused
across exposed south facing coasts.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 5 AM Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory, from 5
AM Monday to 5 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach
erosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most
vulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long
Beach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will
likely be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the
lingering erosion effects enhances the vulnerabilities for
locally more significant coastal flooding.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 26 at 7:27PM PDT until September 28 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf
Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Focused
across exposed south facing coasts.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 5 AM Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory, from 5
AM Monday to 5 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach
erosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most
vulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long
Beach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will
likely be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the
lingering erosion effects enhances the vulnerabilities for
locally more significant coastal flooding.
properties.instruction:

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Sunday, September 27, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Sunday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:
Ozone: The Facts www.tceq.texas.gov/airquality/monops/ozonefacts.html
EPA AirNow: www.airnow.gov/?city=Houston&state=TX&country=USA

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 26 at 12:01PM MST until September 29 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive and long duration rainfall.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn areas, low-water
crossings, creeks, streams, washes and swimming holes. Larger
creeks and rivers may exceed bankfull. Flooding of paved roads and
highway underpasses will be possible. Unpaved roads could become
muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Low pressure will interact with tropical moisture from the
eastern Pacific. This could potentially produce numerous showers
and embedded thunderstorms, with heavy rain that will fall over
saturated soils and burn scars. This could lead to localized
flash flooding and rises on local rivers, such as the Little
Colorado River.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO; Dolores, CO; Gunnison, CO; Hinsdale, CO; La Plata, CO; Montezuma, CO; Ouray, CO; San Juan, CO; San Miguel, CO; Grand, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
